code.originalText: Six-month post-fracture, dementia, and caregiver review

text.paragraph: Six-month post-fracture, dementia, and caregiver review. [S]

Mr. Reagan returns six months after the repair of his right hip fracture. He has had no falls. Home physical therapy finished last month, and he keeps up the home exercise program with supervision. He walks in the house and garden every day with the walker. He had no aches or fever after the zoledronic acid infusion three months ago. The evening restlessness is mild and unchanged. Weekly respite, the home health aide, and caregiver education continue, and the caregiver burden score has fallen. [S]

Continue cholecalciferol 2,000 units daily and calcium from food.
Calcium, phosphorus, and kidney function before the second infusion in about nine months.
Vertebral fracture assessment and FRAX with the next DXA.

History of falling (Z91.81). No falls through six months; Timed Up and Go 16 seconds, improved from 24 but above the 12-second threshold, so fall risk remains increased. [S]
Continue the home exercise program, the walker, and supervision on stairs and at night.

Dementia due to Alzheimer's disease, moderate (FAST stage 5) (F02.B0). Stable, with mild evening restlessness that responds to routine. GDS-15 score 3. Barthel Index 85, the best since the fracture. [S]
Continue donepezil 10 mg each morning.
Yearly dementia review with MoCA, FAST stage, and ADL and IADL scores in about seven months.

Caregiver support. Zarit Burden Interview 27 of 88, down from 41 at the first visit, with weekly respite, the home health aide, and caregiver education. [S]
Continue respite and the aide.
Zarit Burden Interview again at the yearly review.

text.paragraph: Guideline basis: Management of Hip Fractures in Older Adults Evidence-Based Clinical Practice Guideline (2021); The clinician's guide to prevention and treatment of osteoporosis (2022); American Geriatrics Society 2023 updated AGS Beers Criteria for potentially inappropriate medication use in older adults (2023); Alzheimer's Association clinical practice guideline for the Diagnostic Evaluation, Testing, Counseling, and Disclosure of Suspected Alzheimer's Disease and Related Disorders (DETeCD-ADRD) (2024); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, Alzheimer's disease, hip/pelvic fracture, and osteoporosis monographs (2026); Falls Prevention in Community-Dwelling Older Adults: Interventions (2024)

Follow-up: Annual wellness visit in three months. Yearly dementia review in about seven months. Calcium, phosphorus, and kidney function before the second zoledronic acid infusion in about nine months. Next scheduled visit 2026-10-13: subsequent annual wellness visit. [S]
